Day One to Journal 1.1.0-beta.1
Import Day One JSON entries into Apple Journal while keeping a local ledger of imported UUIDs.

Shortcuts generated by Shortcuts Playground. May contain mistakes. Always check the shortcut's actions first.
This shortcut was updated via the following user prompt:
> Okay let's work on fixing the obvious bugs in the shortcut
Choose where import progress is stored. - Use the export folder for a normal import - For reduced batches, choose the folder containing the original ledger
Where is already_imported_uuids.json? For a reduced batch, choose the folder containing your original ledger.
Load the import ledger. - Input uses the ledger in the chosen folder - If a normal export has no ledger yet, start an empty dictionary
Check for Day One JSON files. - Input counts JSON files excluding the import ledger - Stop when the selected folder contains no candidates
No Day One JSON files were found. Choose the unzipped export folder.
Choose the Day One export JSON file
Check the selected export before importing. - Input counts the entries from the chosen JSON - Stop if there are no entries to process
The selected JSON has no entries to import. Check that it is the Day One export, or prepare another batch.
Process the selected Day One entries in order. - Input uses the complete selected entries list - Each UUID is checked against the ledger; no entries are skipped by position
Require an entry identifier before importing. - Input uses the current entry UUID - Stop if it is missing so progress can be recorded reliably
A Day One entry is missing its UUID. Nothing was imported for this entry. Check the export before continuing.
Check if we have already imported this entry
Check the in-memory ledger for this entry UUID. Save the ledger after a successful import.
Skip entries already present in the ledger. - Input uses the lookup result from the in-memory ledger - If it has a value, this entry was already imported
Get the date and the raw entry text, we have to convert it to get the proper timezone relative to when it was written.
Return a ISO 8601 date with the correct timezone ￼for the date ￼
Even if the images are inline, Journal does not support that, so we will fetch the images from the JSON.
Start each entry with its full body. Generated titles must not discard text or reuse a previous entry.
Usually, the first item is a title, but not always.
If the first item is too long, then we don’t have a title, then we will summarize the entry text without photo data.
Decide whether the first line can be used as the title. - Input uses the word count from the title candidate - Long title candidates are replaced with a generated title
Summarize the following text to a title for a journal entry, keep it plain text, no markdown, it should have no more than 12 words in it: ￼
Remove the title line when there is body text below it. - Input uses the number of entry lines - Entries with multiple lines keep the remaining lines as body text
Get Photos for entry. 13 is the limit for number of allowed attachments in Journal.
Check whether this entry has photos. - Input uses the number of photo entries - Entries with photos use the cached export file list
Prepare the export file cache for photo lookup. - Input uses the cached export file list - If it is empty, scan the export folder once now
Limit photos to Journal attachment capacity. - Input uses the number of photo entries - Entries over the limit use the maximum supported photo count
Collect exported photo files for this entry. - Input uses the selected Day One photo records - Matching files are found from the cached export file list
Clear the previous entry’s location before reading this entry. Entries without a location leave these values empty.
Append location details when Day One exported them. - Input uses the Day One location dictionary - Entries with location data add readable place details to the text
Append a weather summary when Day One exported weather. - Input uses the Day One weather dictionary - Entries with weather data generate a readable summary
Summarize the weather the ￼in ￼, ￼, ￼. With ￼on the date ￼. Don't include the weather source. If there is no location data, then say so, don't get data for other locations.
Save the entry to the ledger dictionary to mark it as imported
